requirement_text: Admission to a bachelor's program or the Preparatory School requires: (1) submission of the application within the application deadline; (2) a university entrance qualification certificate, verified by preliminary review documentation (VPD) from uni-assist; (3) language skills at the level required by TU Berlin; and (4) application in the proper form. "Regardless of your nationality, with an international university entrance qualification you must always apply to TU Berlin. This also applies if you are interested in a bachelor's program with open admission (no NC) or if you are already enrolled at TU Berlin and would like to switch to a different bachelor's program."

requirement_text: "In the last application periods, less than 5 % of applicants fulfilled the entry requirements listed below and could be admitted... In particular, the field of Theoretical Computer Science was not covered in most applications. Theoretical Computer Science includes courses i.e. on the topics formal languages, automata, computability, complexity, logic. Courses on discrete structures, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, digital logic, design and analysis of algorithms are not recognized in the field of Theoretical Computer Science."

researcher_notes: Highest-value named-exclusion record in this batch, matching scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md #3 precisely: the 12-CP Theoretical Computer Science sub-requirement explicitly excludes a list of courses (discrete structures, algorithms, data structures, digital logic, etc.) that an applicant would plausibly — and, per TU Berlin's own <5% admit-rate figure, do in practice — assume qualify as 'theoretical CS'. A credit-point count that only checks total CP without checking against this exclusion list would confidently and wrongly tell a student they meet this requirement.

requirement_text: Health insurance is required to enroll (not merely to be admitted). The general requirements page states broadly that "the fifth Social Security Code stipulates that all enrolled students in Germany are required to have statutory health insurance... it is not possible to enrol without health insurance." The bachelor's FAQ states more specifically that "students under 30 are mandated by German law to have health insurance," and that a German health insurance company must send an electronic notification to TU Berlin to enroll.

limitations: Two official TU Berlin pages frame the same underlying German statutory-insurance rule at different levels of precision (general 'all enrolled students' vs. FAQ-specific 'students under 30' mandated for statutory (SGB V) insurance) rather than stating literally conflicting rules; both are recorded rather than silently collapsed into one framing. This is an enrollment requirement rather than an admission requirement in the strict sense, included here because it is a hard gate on completing matriculation.
